text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 9 in history.

1802 - Elijah Parish Lovejoy born. Editor of the St Louis Observer and anti-slavery campaigner who died in 1837 defending his paper when a mob destroyed his building. He became known as the "Martyr Abolitionist".

1818 - Ivan Sergeyevich Turgenev born. Russian novelist, poet and playwright. Best known for his portrayals of Russian rural life, especially in his novel "Fathers and Sons" and his play "A Month in the Country".
1841 - Edward VII of Great Britain born. Eldest son of Queen Victoria, and Prince of Wales until his mother's death in January 1901 when he became king.
1869 - Marie Dressler born. Canadian actress on stage and screen. Best known for her roles in "Min and Bill", for which she won an Oscar, and "Dinner at Eight".

1888 - Jean Monnet born. French political economist and diplomat who, after World War Two, helped to rebuild the western European economy. First president of the European Coal and Steel Community (1952-55).
1888 - Jack the Ripper's fifth and last known victim, Mary Jane Kelly, was found in her room in London's Whitechapel.

1913 - Film actress Hedy Lamarr born in Austria as Hedwig Kiesler. Her films included "Algiers", "Samson and Delilah" and "Boom Town". Also famed for her nude sequence in the 1933 film Exstase (Ecstasy).
1918 - Spiro Agnew born. U.S. politician, resigned as vice president in 1973 rather than stand trial on charges that he had extorted money while serving as governor of Maryland.
1918 - Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany abdicated and a council of People's Delegates assumed power.
1937 - Ramsay MacDonald, who became Britain's first Labour prime minister in 1924, died.

1938 - Anti-Jewish riots took place in much of Germany after the murder of a German official in Paris. The streets of the main cities were littered with glass, and the night became known as "Kristallnacht" (Crystal Night).

1940 - Neville Chamberlain died. British prime minister from 1937, he followed a policy of appeasement with Nazi Germany in the years before World War Two, negotiating the Munich agreement with Adolf Hitler in 1938. Replaced by Winston Churchill in May 1940, he died six months later.
1965 - A huge power failure blacked out New York City, parts of eight northeastern states and parts of Canada, affecting 30 million people.
1967 - The first Saturn V rocket carrying the unmanned Apollo 4 spacecraft was successfully launched from the Kennedy Space Centre.

1970 - Charles De Gaulle, French soldier and statesman, died at 79. The man who symbolised France's resistance to Nazi occupation, he led the French government in exile during World War Two and headed the first government after the LIberation. Later founded the Fifth Republic, served as its first president from 1958 until 1969.
1989 - East Germans on foot and in cars began arriving in West Germany and West Berlin only hours after the East German government threw open its border to the West.
1990 - King Birendra of Nepal proclaimed a new constitution that restored multi-party democracy to the Himalayan kingdom and stripped him of his absolute power.
